description: The National Response Center, staffed by the U.S. Coast Guard, is the federal emergency call centre that receives initial reports of oil spills, chemical releases and maritime security incidents from anyone who witnesses them, and passes them to the responsible agencies; it is not itself a response agency. Its website publishes the reports it has received as yearly Excel files, one per calendar year from 1990 to 2026; their columns were not opened for this record. The files are free to download; further records can be requested under the Freedom of Information Act, and as U.S. Government works they are in the public domain. Caveats: the reports are unverified initial notifications, often with estimated quantities and duplicates, and do not record the outcome of the response. For simulation they form a long event record of hazardous releases from fixed facilities, pipelines, rail and ships for failure-frequency, hazard exposure and emergency response studies. Related catalogue records include the U.S. Chemical Safety Board investigations and the EPA Toxics Release Inventory.
